Please do not merge. I'll split the 1st commit to to its own MR, then follow-up with the other 2.
This should be mentioned in the release notes, since this is a significant change for anyone consuming JSON.
You mean as a separate PR to doc/release-notes.adoc?
Whichever way is easiest.

Wait, for something consuming JSON a relative value "295000" will be either 295000ns *or* 295000s and there's no way to distinguish them? That doesn't seem acceptable.

I think this needs a little more thought. As written, functions call `rel_time_to_secs_str` and then get back a string that might be seconds or might be nanoseconds. There are other functions that might call it as well besides in `ftypes-time.c` (which ultimately affects the JSON.)

Perhaps having a `rel_time_to_nsecs_str` and letting `proto_item_fill_label` decide whether to call that, or perhaps having a return value indicating what kind of string was returned.
There will be a fractional part with some precisions that allows distinguishing them, but not `WS_TSPREC_SEC`.

Related to the problem with JSON, as `epan/ftypes/ftype-time.c relative_val_to_repr` uses `rel_time_to_secs_str`, this would mean that right-clicking on a small `FT_RELATIVE_TIME` (displayed in nanoseconds) like above and selecting "Apply as Filter" would create a filter that filtered for the wrong value (the seconds equivalent).

`relative_val_to_repr` allows returning a different string depending on whether it is for a filter expression or for display, but the printing functions use the display representation. We could switch to the display representation always having the units, but that would be a fairly significant change for consumers of JSON, XML, etc.

Yes, I think overall this attempt is a bit naive and needs some fresh set of ideas. We need to separate display representation - and make it humanally consumable based on the values and other consumers - which I guess even just for backward compatibility, should remain with seconds.

commits_data.title: Display relative time in nanoseconds (if seconds is zero)
commits_data.message:
Display relative time in nanoseconds (if seconds is zero)

Today when we get response time, it's sometimes looks as (example):
[Response time: 0.000129471 seconds]
This is somewhat hard to read, especially for latency which is a sub-seconds metric usually.

This is a straightforwad patch to just print the nanoseconds, in case:
1. Sub-second latency (ns->secs == 0)
2. Positive nanoseconds (ns->nsecs > 0)
3. Precision is in nanoseconds. (precision == WS_TSPREC_NSEC)

Signed-off-by: Yaniv Kaul <mykaul@gmail.com>
Fixes: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/19966
